notes:
Account snapshot: Kestrel builds edge-to-cloud routing and telemetry for last-mile logistics (fleet size ~12k vehicles). Heavy read/write embedding use for route similarity + live reranking for on-device suggestions. High SLA sensitivity because customers are paying per-delivery latency penalties.

Negotiation focus: SLA contract for Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs + throughput guarantees). current status: Redwood commercial and infra teams met with Kestrel on 2026-03-03 to review draft SLA terms. Kestrel legal circulated redlines on 2026-03-07.

Key commercial asks (Kestrel):
- Uptime: require 99.99% monthly uptime for dedicated pool serving production traffic (primary ask).
- Credit schedule: graduated credits: >=99.99 (no credits), 99.95-99.99 -> 10% monthly credit, 99.5-99.95 -> 30% credit, <99.5 -> 100% credit + right to termination after 2 consecutive months. Legal insists on explicit RTO/RPO for data plane.
- Maintenance windows: no planned maintenance between 06:00-22:00 ET (peak). Request: one emergency maintenance allowed with 4h notice; planned maintenance must be >72h notice and occur in agreed weekend blackout exception.
- Support / response times: P1 (production outage impacting >10% fleet) -> 15 min response (initial ack), 1h remediation SLA for command path; P2 -> 1h response, 8h target for workaround. Include named escalation paths and 24/7 dedicated SE post-go-live for first 90 days.
- Throughput and latency SLOs: for canonical model (mix of chat+embeddings): guaranteed baseline throughput = 180 qps for avg payload (512 tokens equivalent). Latency SLOs: p95 latency < 220ms for generation up to 512 tokens; p99 < 400ms. If throughput requirement exceeded, Redwood to provide burst capacity or auto-scale within 5 minutes or agreed surcharge.
- Reserved GPU planning: request reserved pool of 24 H100-80GB or equivalent (quantization allowed) for production; 6 additional GPUs for staging/validation. Procurement wants SKU confirmation and ramp schedule (Q3 pilot -> Q4 steady-state). Pricing model: fixed monthly reservation + per-token overage.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: require policy that routes to smaller quantized variant before rejecting; also require KV cache warmup guarantees after failover.

Redwood position (summary from AE/SE):
- Redwood comfortable with 99.95% standard; willing to ladder to 99.99% with price uplift and firm reserved commit (min 12-month).
- Credit schedule proposal: 5% credit for 99.9-99.95, 25% for 99.0-99.9, 100% <99.0. Kestrel unhappy with thresholds; legal asks for example month calculation methodology.
- Maintenance: Redwood can agree to restricted maintenance but asks for 2 scheduled 2h maintenance windows / month outside peak; emergency patches with 24h notice except security-critical hotfixes.
- Support: Redwood offers P1 30 min initial response with enterprise SLA add-on to reduce to 15 min. Dedicated TAM/SE for first 90 days is OK.
- Throughput: Redwood can guarantee baseline 180 qps for the composed model on recommended hardware (H100 equivalent) with committed concurrency and batching settings; needs production load profile to finalize queue sizing.
- Reserved GPUs: Redwood needs a signed commit to reserve the SKUs; availability constrained by cloud partner inventory; can offer equivalent Ampere-gen if H100 not available with validated perf delta.
